question.problem: Which of the following best describes the projection of the intersection between the elliptic cone $2{x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2}=2(z-2)^{2}$ and the plane $2z-x-10=0$ onto the $xy$-plane?
question.worked_solution:
Since we want to find the projection onto the $xy$-plane, we need to eliminate the variable $z.$ First, we solve the equation of the plane for $z,$ as follows:

$$
2z-x-10=0\,⟹\,z=\frac{x}{2}+5
$$

Substituting the expression for $z$ into the equation of the elliptic cone, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2} & =2{(\frac{x}{2}+5-2)}^{2} \\ 2{x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2} & =2{(\frac{x}{2}+3)}^{2} \\ 2{x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2} & =2(\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+3x+9) \\ 2{x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2} & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+6x+18 \\ \frac{3{x}^{2}}{2}-6x+(y+3)^{2} & =18 \\ \frac{3}{2}({x}^{2}-4x+4)-6+(y+3)^{2} & =18 \\ \frac{3}{2}{(x-2)}^{2}+(y+3)^{2} & =24 \\ \frac{{(x-2)}^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{24} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

This is the equation of an ellipse centered at $(2,-3)$ in the $xy$-plane.
